properties.name: ROOT CAUSE 2026-10-28: a registry holding its full count of open designs runs out of file handles. Its open-design limit and the per-store table-file cap were each chosen alone, and neither was checked against the process's open-file limit
properties.source: ssh read-only measurements on the flo2.io droplet (/proc/<pid>/limits, /proc/<pid>/fd, docker logs reflow2) and a local fd count of the published 0.92.0 and 0.93.0 binaries on one store
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-10-28 16:36 UTC, moving flo2.io to 0.93.0. The upgrade's step 5 opened all 64 designs one after another. The last two, 8a37349fecb055d8 and 76713bdbff6684be, answered HTTP 503 (Retry-After 30). The engine said "Failed to open RocksDB … 000029.sst: Too many open files" for one and "full-text index open failed … TooManyOpenFiles … meta.json" for the other. tantivy's file watcher also failed for 3 designs that were already open. No storage write failed.

MEASURED:
- The engine process had soft RLIMIT_NOFILE 1024 (hard 524288), Docker's default. The container sets no ulimit.
- It held 1,013 file handles with about 62 designs open, about 16 per design.
- On reflow2's own store, the published 0.92.0 and 0.93.0 hold the same: 22 handles per process, 12 of them in the store, over repeated runs. So this is not a regression in 0.93.0.
- When the idle designs closed after 15 minutes, the count fell to 446 and both designs opened (HTTP 200).
- flo2.io's design count reached 64 since 2026-10-26: 57 designs existed before that day, and 7 were made after.

CAUSE (the class): three bounds meet in one process, and nothing compares them.
- --registry-max-open (64 on flo2.io) was set as a MEMORY bound.
- MAX_OPEN_FILES_PER_STORE (64 table files per store, #606) was set per store.
- The process's RLIMIT_NOFILE is whatever the host gives. Docker's default soft limit is 1024.
Their product has no check: 64 designs × up to 64 table files plus WAL and index files can need several thousand handles. Today's designs are small (about 5 table files each), so this held until the design count reached about 62. A design's growth in table files moves the same line.

CANDIDATES REFUTED:
- A regression in 0.93.0: refuted, the per-design count is equal.
- A store damaged by the move: refuted, both designs open once handles free up.
- The registry's busy 503 (every open design serving at once): refuted, the reply text names TooManyOpenFiles.

NOT ESTABLISHED:
- Whether 0.92.0 ever hit this in normal traffic. The old container's logs went with the recreate.
- Whether a RocksDB flush or compaction refused for lack of a handle would leave a store in a background-error state. None was seen.
